methodological_rigor.justification: Case series of 6 relapsed/refractory RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML patients (LoE 5). No comparison group, control arm, or randomization. Small sample size. Retrospective data collection. Statistical methods minimal beyond descriptive reporting.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series reporting preliminary results of novel conditioning regimen. Potentially relevant for future investigation but insufficient evidence for practice guidance. Hematologic malignancy but findings not broadly generalizable.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe conditioning regimen and disease monitoring. Results table-based presentation of individual cases. Lacks systematic adverse event reporting per standardized grading. No data availability discussion.

novelty_literature.justification: First case series of olaparib-enhanced conditioning for this AML subtype. Novel combination but biologically based on known HRR deficiency. Limited mechanistic validation.

writing_presentation.justification: Methods detailed for conditioning. Discussion comprehensive on PARPi mechanisms. Results lack systematic structure. Clarity adequate but organization could improve.

key_strengths: First reported use of olaparib-enhanced conditioning for RUNX1::RUNX1T1+ AML with sound mechanistic rationale
100% complete molecular remission at 3 months in all 6 patients
Feasible and tolerable regimen with successful engraftment
key_concerns: Uncontrolled case series (N=6) with no comparison group prohibits causal inference
Very small sample size limits statistical power; single institutional experience
Median follow-up 25 months insufficient for long-term hematologic endpoints
No mechanistic validation of PARPi efficacy; no functional studies demonstrating HRR deficiency
chief_reviewer.rationale: Early-phase case series reporting promising preliminary results for novel conditioning approach. Insufficient evidence level for independent publication; belongs in preliminary communications or as part of larger prospective trial. Case series design alone falls below peer-reviewed journal threshold.
